beats.intro: Unit six is about graphs. [[q]]Everything starts with a grid that lets you give any point an exact address.
beats.plane: Take a horizontal number line: the x axis. [[y]]Add a vertical number line through its zero: the y axis. [[origin]]They cross at the origin. [[grid]]Together they make the coordinate plane.
beats.pair: Every point has an address called an ordered pair: an x coordinate, then a y coordinate, in parentheses. [[q]]To plot three, four, [[x]]start at the origin and move three to the right, [[y]]then four up. [[dot]]That's the point three, four. [[order]]The order matters. Four, three is a different point: four right, then three up.
beats.neg: Negative coordinates move the other way. [[a]]For negative three, negative five: three to the left, then five down. [[b]]For six, one: six right, one up. [[c]]For negative two, zero: two to the left, and no move up or down. That point sits right on the x axis.
beats.quad: The axes split the plane into four quadrants. They're numbered counterclockwise, starting at the top right. [[q1]]Quadrant one: x positive, y positive. [[q2]]Quadrant two: x negative, y positive. [[q3]]Quadrant three: both negative. [[q4]]Quadrant four: x positive, y negative. [[axis]]Points on an axis, like negative two, zero, are not in any quadrant.
beats.relation: A set of ordered pairs is called a relation. [[q]]Take negative five, one; negative two, zero; one, negative one; four, negative two; and seven, negative three. [[dom]]The domain is the set of all the x coordinates: negative five, negative two, one, four, seven. [[rng]]The range is the set of all the y coordinates: negative three up to one. [[braces]]We write sets inside curly braces, usually in order from least to greatest.
beats.wrap: Points on the coordinate plane are written as ordered pairs: [[w1]]x first, how far right or left, then y, how far up or down. [[w2]]The four quadrants are numbered counterclockwise from the top right. [[w3]]The domain of a relation is its set of x values, and the range is its set of y values. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
beats.final1: Chapter practice. Name the quadrant or axis for each point.
beats.final3: Last one. Find the domain and range.
beats.finish: Well done. That's the end of chapter thirty-one, points and lines.
